fault: The keyboard has an unspecified problem that is not tied to any single key.
diagnosis: You haven't named a specific key, so I can't tell which part is faulty. I'll walk you through a safe general check: power it down, look for debris or damage, then reconnect and test.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before touching anything inside the keyboard.
Touch grounded metal first to discharge static before handling the board.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal before you reach for the board.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while handling the keyboard.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

steps.title: Inspect the cable port
steps.instruction: Look into the USB-C port at the back of the keyboard. Check that it is clean and not bent or loose.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is visible and the camera sees no debris, bent metal or cracks around it.
common_mistakes: Skipping the port check and blaming the keys.
Poking inside the port with a metal object.

steps.title: Blow out dust
steps.instruction: Hold the keyboard level and blow compressed air across the keys and gaps. Work from one side to the other.
steps.expected_visual_state: Compressed air is aimed at the keyboard surface and no dust or crumbs remain between the keys.
common_mistakes: Shaking the keyboard upside down and spreading debris inside.
Spraying liquid cleaner instead of using compressed air.

steps.title: Reconnect and test
steps.instruction: Plug the USB-C cable back in. Press a few keys in a text editor or online keyboard tester to see what still fails.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is on, and typed characters appear on the screen.
common_mistakes: Not noting which key or behavior still fails so you can tell me next.
